subject: Materials Science
title: Wear: Surfaces in Battle
description: A quick win: understand Wear: Surfaces in Battle.

hook.text: A car engine piston slides billions of times — without wear resistance, it'd be scrap in a week.

buildup.text: Wear removes material from surfaces in contact — abrasion, adhesion, erosion, or fretting.

discovery.text: Archard's law says wear volume is proportional to load and sliding distance, inversely to hardness.

twist.text: Harder isn't always better — brittle hard surfaces can fracture and wear faster than tough soft ones.

climax.text: Surface treatments — nitriding, carburizing, coatings — harden where wear happens without making the bulk brittle.

punchline.text: Wear is a surface problem — solve it at the surface.

quiz.question: According to Archard's law, what reduces wear?
